query: Which low-cost versus long-term shelter interventions should be costed and prioritised, which municipal or agency actors are responsible, and what measurable indicators (e.g., % vulnerable within 30 min) will track impact?

response.query: Which low-cost versus long-term shelter interventions should be costed and prioritised, which municipal or agency actors are responsible, and what measurable indicators (e.g., % vulnerable within 30 min) will track impact?
response.answer: Low-cost shelters should prioritize immediate needs, while long-term shelters focus on sustainable solutions; municipal housing authorities and social services agencies are typically responsible, with measurable indicators including % of vulnerable populations within 30 minutes of shelter access.

results.title: Scaling Up Biodiversity-Positive Incentives
results.content: For example, many of the privately financed PES schemes have focused on changing upstream land-use practices to improve water quality and quantity downstream, with payments made by beverage companies, breweries, hydropower companies and water utilities [(Ezzine-de-Blas et al., 2016[24])](/en/publications/scaling-up-biodiversity-positive-incentives_19b859ce-en/full-report/biodiversity-positive-subsidies-and-payments-for-ecosystem-services_b571702b.html#CrossRef_wR29HA4QsR3PTUs0X6tngQ_365e56f81e). Several PES schemes that leverage private finance have included a focus on carbon [(Ezzine-de-Blas et al., 2016[24])](/en/publications/scaling-up-biodiversity-positive-incentives_19b859ce-en/full-report/biodiversity-positive-subsidies-and-payments-for-ecosystem-services_b571702b.html#CrossRef_wR29HA4QsR3PTUs0X6tngQ_365e56f81e). The establishment of trust funds or use of existing administrative structures can help reduce transaction costs for private sector actors wishing to contribute to a PES scheme [(Engel, Pagiola and Wunder, 2008[8])](/en/publications/scaling-up-biodiversity-positive-incentives_19b859ce-en/full-report/biodiversity-positive-subsidies-and-payments-for-ecosystem-services_b571702b.html#CrossRef_Nar5ZbsVWUVIobrqIJtFbQ_365e56f81e). An analysis of the effectiveness of different payment schemes using field parameterised, ecological economic models of extensive grazing farms in the UK concluded that potential biodiversity benefits from improved spatial targeting and payment differentiation were sufficiently high to warrant an increase in implementations costs of 70% [(Armsworth et al., 2012[135])](/en/publications/scaling-up-biodiversity-positive-incentives_19b859ce-en/full-report/biodiversity-positive-subsidies-and-payments-for-ecosystem-services_b571702b.html#CrossRef_7huSj8JeDboczXiEcQzoQg_365e56f81e). When designing payment schemes it is important to identify which approach strikes a balance across cost effectiveness, environmental outcomes, and participants’ preferences [(OECD, 2022[121])](/en/publications/scaling-up-biodiversity-positive-incentives_19b859ce-en/full-report/biodiversity-positive-subsidies-and-payments-for-ecosystem-services_b571702b.html#Kappa_4cf10d76_365e56f81e).
